NEW SECTION . 598A.1 Short title. 1 This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Uniform 2 Family Law Arbitration Act” . 3 Sec. 2. NEW SECTION . 598A.2 Definitions. 4 As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise 5 requires: 6 1. “Arbitration agreement” means an agreement which subjects 7 a family law dispute to arbitration. 8 2. “Arbitration organization” means an association, 9 agency, board, commission, or other entity which is neutral 10 and initiates, sponsors, or administers an arbitration or is 11 involved in the selection of an arbitrator. 12 3. “Arbitrator” means an individual selected or appointed, 13 alone or with others, to make an award in a family law dispute 14 which is subject to an arbitration agreement. 15 4. “Award” means an interim award, temporary order, or final 16 disposition of a family law dispute by an arbitrator. 17 5. “Child custody dispute” means a family law dispute 18 regarding legal custody, physical custody, parenting plans, 19 parenting time, or visitation of a child. 20 6. “Child support dispute” means a family law dispute 21 regarding financial support of a child. 22 7. “Court” means a district court which has jurisdiction 23 over a family law dispute. 24 8. “Family law dispute” means a contested issue arising 25 under chapter 598, 600B, or 600C. “Family law dispute” does not 26 include an issue under section 598A.3, subsection 2. 27 9. “Party” means an individual who signs an arbitration 28 agreement and whose rights will be determined by an award. 29 10. “Person” means an individual, estate, business 30 or nonprofit entity, public corporation, government or 31 governmental subdivision, agency, or instrumentality or any 32 other legal entity. 33 To execute or adopt a tangible symbol. 12 b. NEW SECTION . 598A.3 Scope. 20 1. Except as provided in subsection 2, this chapter governs 21 arbitration of a family law dispute. 22 2. This chapter does not authorize an arbitrator to make an 23 award that does any of the following: 24 a. Grants legal separation, divorce, dissolution of 25 marriage, or annulment. 26 b. Terminates parental rights. 27 c. Grants an adoption or a guardianship of a child or 28 protected person. 29 d. Determines the status of dependency of a child under 30 chapter 232. 31 e. Determines the support of a child under chapter 252B, 32 252E, 252F, or 252H, or if support payments have been assigned 33 to the department of health and human services pursuant to 34 section 234.39 or 239B.6. 35 -2- LSB 5935XC (2) 91 lh/jh 2/ 19 S.F. _____ Sec. 4. NEW SECTION . 598A.4 Applicable law. 1 1. a. Subject to paragraph “b” , the law applicable to 2 arbitration is chapter 679A. 3 b. If there is a conflict between chapter 679A and this 4 chapter, this chapter controls. 5 2. In determining the merits of a family law dispute, an 6 arbitrator shall apply the law of this state, including its 7 choice of law rules. 8 Sec. 5. NEW SECTION . 598A.5 Arbitration agreements. 9 1. An arbitration agreement must do the following: 10 a. Be in a record signed by the parties. 11 b. Identify the arbitrator, an arbitration organization, or 12 a method of selecting an arbitrator. 13 c. Identify the family law dispute the parties intend to 14 arbitrate. 15 2. Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3, an 16 agreement in a record to arbitrate a family law dispute that 17 arises between the parties before, at the time, or after 18 the agreement is made is valid and enforceable as any other 19 contract and irrevocable except on a ground that exists at law 20 or in equity for the revocation of a contract. 21 3. An agreement to arbitrate a child custody dispute or 22 child support dispute that arises between the parties after the 23 agreement is made is unenforceable unless any of the following 24 apply: 25 a. The parties affirm the agreement in a record after the 26 dispute arises. 27 b. The agreement was entered during a family law proceeding 28 and the court approved or incorporated the agreement in an 29 order issued in the proceeding. 30 4. If a party objects to arbitration on the grounds the 31 arbitration agreement is unenforceable or the agreement does 32 not include a family law dispute, the court shall decide 33 whether the agreement is enforceable or includes the family law 34 dispute. 35 -3- LSB 5935XC (2) 91 lh/jh 3/ 19 S.F. _____ Sec. 6. NEW SECTION . 598A.6 Notice of arbitration. 1 A party shall initiate arbitration by giving notice to 2 arbitrate to the other party in the manner specified in the 3 arbitration agreement or, in the absence of a specified manner, 4 under section 679A.15. 5 Sec. 7. NEW SECTION . 598A.7 Motion for judicial relief. 6 1. A motion for judicial relief under this chapter shall be 7 made to the court in which a proceeding is pending involving a 8 family law dispute subject to arbitration or, if no proceeding 9 is pending, a court with jurisdiction over the parties and the 10 subject matter. 11 2. On motion by a party, the court may compel arbitration 12 if the parties have entered into an arbitration agreement that 13 complies with section 598A.5 unless the court determines under 14 section 598A.12 that the arbitration should not proceed. 15 3. On motion of a party, the court shall terminate 16 arbitration if the court determines any of the following: 17 a. The agreement to arbitrate is unenforceable. 18 b. NEW SECTION . 598A.12 Protection of party or child. 9 1. a. This subsection applies if a party is subject 10 to a protection order or the arbitrator determines there 11 is a reasonable basis to believe a party is the victim of 12 domestic violence or a party’s safety or ability to participate 13 effectively in arbitration is otherwise at risk. 14 b. NEW SECTION . 598A.13 Powers and duties of 4 arbitrator. 5 1. An arbitrator shall conduct an arbitration in a manner 6 the arbitrator considers appropriate for a fair and expeditious 7 disposition of the family law dispute. 8 2. An arbitrator shall provide each party a right to be 9 heard, to present evidence material to the family law dispute, 10 and to cross-examine witnesses. 11 3. Unless the parties otherwise agree in a record, an 12 arbitrator may do all of the following: 13 a. Select the rules for conducting the arbitration. 14 b. Hold a conference with the parties before a hearing. 15 c. Determine the date, time, and place of a hearing. 16 d. Require a party to provide all of the following: 17 (1) A copy of a relevant court order. 18 (2) Information required to be disclosed in a family law 19 proceeding under chapters 598 and 600B and the applicable Iowa 20 rules of civil procedure. 21 (3) A proposed award which addresses each issue in 22 arbitration. 23 e. Interview a child who is the subject of a child custody 24 dispute. 25 f. Appoint a private expert at the expense of the parties. 26 g. Administer an oath or affirmation and issue a subpoena 27 for the attendance of a witness or the production of documents 28 and other evidence at a hearing. 29 h. Permit and compel discovery concerning the family law 30 dispute and determine the date, time, and place of discovery. 31 i. Determine the admissibility and weight of evidence. 32 j. Permit deposition of a witness for use as evidence at a 33 hearing. 34 k. For good cause, prohibit a party from disclosing 35 -8- LSB 5935XC (2) 91 lh/jh 8/ 19 S.F. _____ information. 1 l. Appoint an attorney, guardian ad litem, or other 2 representative for a child at the expense of the parties. 3 m. Impose a procedure to protect a party or child from risk 4 of harm, harassment, or intimidation. 5 n. Allocate arbitration fees, attorney fees, expert witness 6 fees, and other costs to the parties. 7 o. Impose a sanction on a party for bad faith or misconduct 8 during the arbitration according to standards governing 9 imposition of a sanction for litigant misconduct in a family 10 law proceeding. 11 4. An arbitrator shall not allow ex parte communication 12 except to the extent allowed in a family law proceeding for 13 communication with a judge. 14 Sec. 14. If an arbitration agreement was made before the effective 9 date of this Act, the parties may agree in a record that this 10 chapter applies to the arbitration. 11 EXPLANATION 12 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 13 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 14 This bill creates the Iowa uniform family law arbitration 15 Act. The bill provides definitions, including the terms 16 “arbitrator”, “child custody dispute”, “child support dispute”, 17 and “family law dispute”. 18 The bill governs the arbitration in a family dispute but does 19 not allow an arbitrator to grant a legal separation, a divorce, 20 a dissolution of marriage, or an annulment; to terminate 21 parental rights, to grant an adoption or a guardianship of 22 a child or protected person; or to determine the status of 23 dependency of a child or the support of a child. 24 The bill provides that an arbitration agreement must be in 25 a record signed by the parties. The agreement must identify 26 the arbitrator, an arbitration organization, or a method of 27 selecting an arbitrator and identify the family law dispute 28 the parties intend to arbitrate. The bill provides that a 29 family law dispute that arises after the arbitration agreement 30 is made unenforceable unless the parties affirm the agreement 31 in a record after the dispute arises or the agreement was 32 entered during a family law proceeding and the court approved 33 or incorporated the agreement in an order issued in the 34 proceeding. If there is an objection to the arbitration 35 -15- LSB 5935XC (2) 91 lh/jh 15/ 19 S.F. _____ agreement on the grounds that it is unenforceable or the 1 agreement does not involve a family dispute, the court shall 2 determine whether it is enforceable or includes an appropriate 3 dispute. 4 The bill provides that notice for arbitration shall be made 5 either in a manner agreed upon or by Code section 679A.15 6 (arbitration —— applications to district court). 7 The bill requires motions for judicial relief to be filed 8 with the court with the appropriate jurisdiction. A party 9 may file a motion to compel arbitration by the court. The 10 bill also allows a party to file a motion for judicial relief 11 to terminate an arbitration. The bill allows upon motion 12 of a party for the court to order consolidation of separate 13 arbitrations involving the same parties and a common issue 14 of law or fact if necessary for resolution of the family law 15 dispute. 16 The bill provides that an arbitrator must be an attorney at 17 law, a former attorney at law on inactive status, or a retired 18 judge and have successfully completed a combined five hours of 19 instruction in an accredited continuing legal education course 20 on domestic violence and child abuse. 21 The bill requires an arbitrator to disclose any information 22 a reasonable person would believe would affect the arbitrator’s 23 impartiality. The arbitrator, the attorneys, and parties are 24 all required to disclose information that would change the 25 impartiality of the arbitrator or the arbitrator’s ability 26 to make a timely award. The bill provides that if a timely 27 disclosure was not made, a party may file a motion to suspend 28 the arbitration no later than 15 days after such failure. The 29 bill provides that failure to disclose can also result in 30 the vacating of an award and other appropriate relief. Upon 31 discharge of an arbitrator, the parties may select a new 32 arbitrator or request that the court select one. 33 The bill allows a party to an arbitration to be represented 34 by counsel, be accompanied by an individual who will not be 35 -16- LSB 5935XC (2) 91 lh/jh 16/ 19 S.F. _____ used as a witness or advocate, and to fully participate in the 1 arbitration. Parties are not allowed to communicate ex parte 2 with the arbitrator. 3 The bill provides that prior to the selection of an 4 arbitrator, the court may enter a temporary order for the 5 family law dispute. After the selection of an arbitrator, the 6 arbitrator may make a temporary award. 7 The bill provides that if a party is subject to a protection 8 order and the arbitrator determines there is a reasonable 9 basis to believe a party is the victim of domestic violence 10 or a party’s safety or ability to participate effectively in 11 arbitration is otherwise at risk, the arbitrator shall stay the 12 arbitration and refer the parties to court. The arbitration 13 shall not resume until the party at risk affirms the agreement 14 in a record and the court determines that the affirmation is 15 informed and voluntary, the arbitration is not inconsistent 16 with the protection order, and reasonable procedures are 17 in place to protect the party. The bill provides that if 18 an arbitrator reasonably believes that a child subject to 19 the matter is abused or neglected, the arbitration shall be 20 terminated and the abuse or neglect shall be reported to the 21 court or another appropriate authority. 22 The bill requires that the arbitrator conduct the 23 arbitration in a manner considered appropriate for a fair and 24 expeditious disposition. The bill provides the arbitrator the 25 following powers: to select the rules for the arbitration; 26 conduct the prehearing conferences and the hearing; administer 27 oaths to parties and witnesses; allow any party to conduct 28 prehearing discovery by interrogatories, deposition, requests 29 for production of documents, or other means; determine the 30 admissibility of evidence; and subpoena witnesses or documents 31 upon the arbitrator’s own initiative or request of a party; the 32 power to meet with a child, appoint a representative for the 33 child, and impose procedures to protect a party or child from 34 risk of harm; and to sanction bad faith conduct according to 35 -17- LSB 5935XC (2) 91 lh/jh 17/ 19 S.F. _____ state law governing misconduct in family law proceedings. 1 The bill does not require an arbitration hearing to be 2 recorded. 3 The bill provides that an award shall be made in a record, 4 dated and signed by the arbitrator and the parties shall be 5 given notice. An award is not enforceable as a judgment until 6 confirmed by the court. 7 The bill requires the court to confirm an award given by 8 an arbitrator. The court shall confirm an award if all the 9 parties agree in a record to confirmation or the time period to 10 correct an unconfirmed award or vacate an award has expired. 11 The bill provides that if an award relates to a child custody 12 dispute or a child support dispute, the court shall confirm 13 the award if the court finds that the award complies with the 14 bill and Code chapter 598 (dissolution of marriage and domestic 15 relations) or 600B (paternity and obligation for support) and 16 is in the best interests of the child.
